Team — quick legal analysis and three drafting options below. High-level position: we should avoid an unlimited carve-out for lost profits or goodwill. Carve-outs tied to a narrow set of triggers (gross negligence/willful misconduct; confirmed unauthorized access to customer data) with a specific monetary floor or alternate cap are more acceptable. Also propose explicit definitions for "loss of data" remediation categories.

Option A (Customer-first — broad carve-out with alternate cap):
"Notwithstanding Section X (Limitation of Liability), Customer may recover damages for (i) costs reasonably incurred to investigate and remediate unauthorized access to Customer Data, (ii) reasonably documented lost profits directly resulting from an incident of unauthorized access to Customer Data, and (iii) documented costs of notification and regulatory fines to the extent resulting from Redwood's gross negligence or willful misconduct. For the avoidance of doubt, damages recoverable under this paragraph shall be subject to an alternate cap equal to the greater of Six Million United States Dollars (USD $6,000,000) or two (2) times the Fees paid by Customer to Redwood in the twelve (12) months preceding the event."

Option B (Balanced compromise — limited, specific carve-outs):
"Notwithstanding Section X, Customer may recover direct damages arising from (i) remediation of confirmed unauthorized access to Customer Data (including forensics, restoration, and notification), and (ii) documented lost profits directly and demonstrably caused by such unauthorized access, provided that Redwood's liability for such damages shall not exceed the greater of One Million United States Dollars (USD $1,000,000) or the Fees paid by Customer to Redwood in the twelve (12) months preceding the event. Loss of goodwill and reputational harm shall only be recoverable where Customer demonstrates, by clear and convincing evidence, that such loss was proximately caused by Redwood's gross negligence or willful misconduct."

Option C (Provider-protective — carve-out for data restoration only):
"Notwithstanding Section X, the limitation of liability shall not apply to reasonable and documented costs to investigate and remediate confirmed unauthorized access to Customer Data (including forensics and restoration). All other categories of consequential or indirect damages, including lost profits and loss of goodwill, remain excluded. The aggregate liability for remediation costs under this paragraph shall be capped at Five Hundred Thousand United States Dollars (USD $500,000)."

Drafting notes and definitions to attach: short definition for "Confirmed unauthorized access" and an itemized remediation cost schedule (forensics, data restoration, notification, credit monitoring). See attached word doc with redlines and a short Annex-A with example damages buckets.

Recommendation: push Option B with a modest increase to the cap (1x fees or $1M whichever greater). That balances Novus' need for meaningful recovery while controlling Redwood's exposure. If Novus insists on lost profits without demonstrable causation, escalate to Markus for commercial sign-off.

Laura Bennett
